From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>

Cc: Sara Klein <sara.klein@credify.com>, Tim O'Neill <tim.oneill@credify.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden drop in reserved throughput — urgent

Evelyn / Ben / Sara —

Initial findings from the runtime logs: around 07:40 PDT we saw a sudden uptick in scheduled jobs on the GPU cluster hosting Credify's reserved pool. Two signals look suspicious:
- A model variant (v3.2-beta) was auto-rolled into a small fraction of serving lanes for A/B traffic. The variant increases memory pressure and causes longer kernel times.
- Concurrent short-lived hosted jobs (non-reserved) were routed to the same host due to a transient routing rule. Those jobs were not supposed to co-locate with reserved tenants.

Immediate mitigation I can apply now (low-risk, quick):
1) Pin Credify's pool to the stable model variant (v3.1) — prevents the memory-pressure behavior.
2) Evict non-reserved short jobs from the host group and trigger re-scheduling to dedicated shared pools.
3) Open a temporary reserved burst window (requires ops + billing approval) to absorb backlog while we stabilize.

I've attached a short playback trace (playback-trace-07030.txt) with the scheduling events and kernel latencies.

I can perform steps 1 and 2 immediately; step 3 needs authorization. Estimated time to measurable improvement after 1+2 is ~6–9 minutes.

Irene Choi
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
